question: C16-S1 + C16-S2 (Bence 2026-11-17: "go 1 2"; train embryos only, exploratory, no claim). C16-S1 = time-varying-rate control, script c16s1_time.py (imports c16s0_hidden.py): P/L rates vary by tree-depth bin; does the hidden state z still beat a depth-varying model without z (held-out per leaf, LOEO)? C16-S2 = link posterior z to expression, script c16s2_link.py (imports c16s0_hidden.py, c14s0_gate.py, c14s3_region.py, c14s4_genes.py, c14s1_select.py): within each observed label (P or L), does the leave-self-out posterior z (relatives' signal) correlate with the expression PCs, per embryo, LOEO; descriptive per-embryo pattern only (no stage contrast claim). Both on Actions (--petracer). Previous step: C16-S0 (Bence 2026-11-17: "Yes, start it" = train-only exploratory fit of a state-transition model with an inherited-state term on the embryo train trees): script c16s0_hidden.py on Actions (--petracer). On the train trees, mesoderm leaves labelled paraxial (P) or lateral plate (L); M0 = 2-state continuous-time Markov model of P/L along the tree; M1 = adds a hidden inherited binary state z (switch rate mu) that sets the P/L transition rates. Leave-one-embryo-out held-out log-likelihood per leaf, M1 vs M0; fitted mu gives the memory half-life in tree edges. Expression is NOT used (the link to the C14-S4 program is a later step). No sealed data (A spent, B and C sealed); exploratory chapter: no sealed test, so the H19 power gate does not apply and no claim can come from it. RESULT 2026-11-17 (run 44082919451): smokes PASS; held-out gain +0.037/leaf, 6/6 embryos positive -> memory term SUPPORTED (exploratory, no claim); half-life about 12 edges, near-absorbing fate bias. Open alternatives: clade-level niche, time-varying rates.

value: C16: first mechanistic model fit since chapter 6 (goal: model fate behaviour). Tests whether a hidden inherited state, beyond the observed lineage label, is needed to explain how paraxial vs lateral-plate fates are distributed on whole-embryo trees, and estimates how many divisions it persists (memory half-life). C14 showed state beyond type predicts relatives' fate (confirmed on A) and C14-S5 ruled out type impurity; this asks for the mechanism-level description. Exploratory: no powered sealed partition is left (B underpowered, C last reserve). C15: brings the mechanistic model back (goal: model fate behaviour). A fitted state-transition model on lineage trees with an inherited-state term (C14-S4/S5 origin program, now justified beyond type impurity), tested on sealed hosts of an in vivo growth model; the source study could not determine transition directionality, and no paper we read tests state beyond cluster on held-out units (#12 methods, #25). 32 hosts give fresh sealed partitions. C14: first sealed, out-of-embryo test that state beyond cell type predicts clade fate in a living mammalian embryo; extends confirmed chapters 7, 8, 10 (culture) in vivo. Lineage inpainting 2026 predicts from lineage context without held-out embryos; overlap low per source headings. Exposure: two re-analysis abstracts (lineage inpainting, scPFA), topic level. Earlier value (C9): Chromatin counterpart of chapter 8's confirmed RNA T1 (rho 0.45): a clone's day-2.5 accessibility predicting its specific Neu/Mono split on unseen clones. Jindal 2024 reports chromatin fate priming at population level, not a sealed clone-level split prediction; adds a disciplined replication in a second modality, value modest.
literature: C16: model class = continuous-time Markov models of discrete traits on trees with a hidden rate class (hidden-rates / covarion-type models, standard in comparative phylogenetics); applied to cell lineage trees by Yang et al. 2022 (#12; parsimony transitions, directionality undetermined) and Quantitative fate mapping 2022 (C14 seed); Gowri et al. 2026 (#25) fits no mechanistic model. No new paper read for C16-S0. C15: Yang et al.
